title: nvvm_ldu_global_{i,f,p} align operand read via unguarded cast<ConstantInt> in getTgtMemIntrinsic — operand is not ImmArg, crashes on runtime align
trigger: Call @llvm.nvvm.ldu.global.i.i32.p0 (or .f / .p variants) with a non-constant value for the second (alignment) argument.

title: Top-level large-integer (iN, N>64, N not a multiple of 8) global drops its high partial byte
trigger: Any module-scope global of integer type with bit width > 64 that is not a multiple of 8 and whose top (width%8) bits are nonzero, in addrspace(1) global or addrspace(4) const, with a non-zero/non-undef initializer.

title: PerformSELECTShiftCombine drops i64 shift-amount guard but PTX clamp only sees low 32 bits of amount
trigger: Any well-defined i64 (or wider scalar lowered through this combine) guarded logical shift where the runtime shift amount has a nonzero bit above bit 31 while its low 32 bits are < 64. Example: x=any, s=0x100000005 (=4294967301). IR `s >= 64 ? 0 : x >> s` must yield 0; emitted PTX yields x >> 5.

title: fptosi/fptoui to i1 lowered as (x == 0.0) — inverted, wrong operation for ALL float source types (f16/bf16/f32/f64)
trigger: Any `fptoui`/`fptosi` from f16, bf16, f32, or f64 to i1 with a value in the defined (non-overflowing) range. Reachable from clean IR; confirmed not optimized away.

title: combineMulWide: sext(shl nsw x, bits-1) folds to mul.wide.s with a top-bit-set narrow constant, negating the result
trigger: -O1/-O2/-O3 (combine disabled at -O0). Requires SIGN_EXTEND of an nsw SHL whose constant shift amount equals the source type width minus 1 (15 for i16->i32, 31 for i32->i64). ZERO_EXTEND/nuw is unaffected (MUL_WIDE_UNSIGNED zero-extends). Shift amounts < bits-1 are fine (top bit clear).

title: NVPTXLowerArgs ArgUseChecker treats atomicrmw on a byval kernel param as read-only -> missing local copy (miscompile) / convertToParamAS crash
mechanism:
ArgUseChecker (PtrUseVisitor<ArgUseChecker>) decides whether a byval kernel param is only read. It overrides visitStoreInst/AddrSpaceCast/PtrToInt/PHI/Select/MemTransfer/MemSet, but does NOT override visitAtomicRMWInst. InstVisitor dispatches AtomicRMWInst -> visitAtomicRMWInst -> DELEGATE(Instruction) -> visitInstruction, and neither ArgUseChecker nor PtrUseVisitor overrides visitInstruction, so it falls to InstVisitor's no-op default `void visitInstruction(Instruction &I) {}`. Result: an `atomicrmw` (a WRITE) neither aborts nor escapes the visit, so `const bool ArgUseIsReadOnly = !(PI.isEscaped() || PI.isAborted());` (line 436) is TRUE. Two wrong outcomes follow:
(a) Direct use (no phi/select): case 1 at line 437 fires (`ArgUseIsReadOnly && AUC.Conditionals.empty()`), convertToParamAS() is called on the atomicrmw, which is not Load/GEP/BitCast/ASC/MemTransfer, hitting `llvm_unreachable("Unsupported instruction")` at line 256 -> compiler abort.
(b) Use behind a select/phi on an sm70+/ptx>=7.7 target: Conditionals is non-empty so case 1 is skipped, then case 2 at line 448 (`HasCvtaParam && (ArgUseIsReadOnly || isParamGridConstant)`) fires because ArgUseIsReadOnly is (wrongly) true. The arg is lowered via cvta.param, marked ReadOnly, and NO per-thread local copy is made (copyByValParam at line 470 is never reached). The emitted PTX does `mov.b64 %rd1, k_param_0; cvta.param.u64 %rd4, %rd1; atom...add.u32 [%rd4],1`, i.e. the atomic add hits the single shared param-space copy. byval semantics require each thread to operate on a private copy, so instead of each thread independently computing old=0,new=1, all N threads atomically accumulate into the same location (result N / data race) -> wrong result for a well-defined input. Verified both manifestations with llc.
trigger: A non-grid_constant `byval` pointer kernel argument used by `atomicrmw`. (a) crash: used directly. (b) miscompile: used via a select/phi together with another pointer, compiled for sm_70+ with PTX>=7.7 (cvta.param available).
llc_cmd: llc -mtriple=nvptx64 -mcpu=sm_90a -mattr=+ptx80 in.ll -o -   (miscompile: @miscompile emits cvta.param + atom on shared param mem, no local copy); llc -mtriple=nvptx64 -mcpu=sm_70 in.ll -o -   (crash: @crash hits llvm_unreachable at NVPTXLowerArgs.cpp:256)

title: combineMulWide: sext(shl nsw x, bits-1) fabricates a top-bit-set narrow constant fed to MUL_WIDE_SIGNED, negating the result
mechanism: For (sign_extend (shl nsw x, K)), combineMulWide rewrites to MUL_WIDE_SIGNED(x, 1<<K) where the multiplier constant is built in the NARROW type: `MulVal = APInt(FromVT.getSizeInBits(), 1) << ShiftAmt; RHS = getConstant(MulVal, DL, FromVT)`. When ShiftAmt == FromVT.bits-1, MulVal has its top bit set (e.g. i32: 0x80000000), which as a signed narrow value is INT_MIN (-2147483648), and mul.wide.s32 SIGN-EXTENDS that constant. But the original sext(shl nsw x, bits-1) is only well-defined (non-poison) for x in {0,-1}; for x=-1 the true value is sext(INT_MIN) = -2^31 = -2147483648, whereas mul.wide.s32(-1, -2147483648) = +2147483648. The guard only checks Op->getFlags().hasNoSignedWrap() (line 6373) and never verifies the fabricated constant is representable as a signed narrow value (unlike the sibling TryMULWIDECombine which guards with Val.isSignedIntN(OptSize) and correctly bails). The unsigned/nuw path is fine; only the signed shl-by-(bits-1) path negates the result. Same defect for i16->i32 (shl by 15 -> mul.wide.s16 ..., -32768).
trigger: sext to i32/i64 of an `shl nsw` by (narrow_bits - 1), e.g. `sext i32 (shl nsw i32 %x, 31) to i64` with %x = -1; or `sext i16 (shl nsw i16 %x, 15) to i32`.

title: PerformSELECTShiftCombine: i64 guarded shift lowered to PTX clamp shift using only the low 32 bits of the i64 shift amount
mechanism: PerformSELECTShiftCombine matches `amt > BitWidth-1 ? 0 : (x >> amt)` (and the ULT form) and rewrites to NVPTXISD::SRL_CLAMP/SHL_CLAMP: `getNode(ClampOpc, ..., ShiftOp.getValueType(), ShiftOp.getOperand(0), ShiftOp.getOperand(1))`. For an i64 value the SHIFT/CLAMP instruction's shift-amount operand is hard-coded to 32 bits (NVPTXInstrInfo.td: SHIFT multiclass uses B32 for the amount, comment: "dest and src may be int64/int32/int16, but shift is always int32"). PTX shr.u64/shl.b64 clamp the 32-bit amount to 64 when >= 64, but the i64 amount is TRUNCATED to 32 bits BEFORE clamping. So the guard `amt > 63` (which is true for amt = 2^32) is dropped, and the clamp instruction sees low32(2^32) = 0, producing `shr.u64 x, 0 = x` instead of the guarded 0. llc emits `ld.param.b32 %r1, [param_1]` then `shr.u64 %rd2, %rd1, %r1`, confirming only the low 32 bits of the i64 amount are used.
trigger: i64 (or any >32-bit) guarded logical shift where the runtime shift amount has nonzero bits above bit 31 but its low 32 bits are < BitWidth, e.g. amt = 0x100000000 (2^32): correct result is 0 (guard true), emitted result is x (shifts by 0).

title: NVPTXLowerArgs ArgUseChecker treats cmpxchg on a byval kernel param as read-only -> missing local copy (miscompile) / convertToParamAS crash
mechanism: Same root cause as the atomicrmw case: ArgUseChecker does not override visitAtomicCmpXchgInst. AtomicCmpXchgInst -> DELEGATE(Instruction) -> visitInstruction, which is the inherited no-op default, so a `cmpxchg` (a conditional WRITE) is classified as read-only (ArgUseIsReadOnly true at line 436). Same two outcomes: direct use takes case 1 -> convertToParamAS() crashes at the `llvm_unreachable` on line 256; use behind a select/phi on sm70+/ptx>=7.7 takes case 2 (line 448) and lowers the byval param with cvta.param, marks it ReadOnly, and skips the per-thread local copy, so the compare-and-swap writes the shared param-space copy seen by every thread instead of a private per-thread copy. Verified: with a select, debug prints "Using non-copy pointer to ptr %input" (case 2) and the PTX uses cvta.param with no local depot copy; direct use crashes at line 256.
trigger: A non-grid_constant `byval` pointer kernel argument used by `cmpxchg`. Crash if used directly; miscompile if used via a select/phi on sm_70+/PTX>=7.7.
llc_cmd: llc -mtriple=nvptx64 -mcpu=sm_90a -mattr=+ptx80 in.ll -o -   (miscompile: @mc_cmpxchg -> cvta.param, no local copy); llc -mtriple=nvptx64 -mcpu=sm_70 in.ll -o -   (crash: @crash_cmpxchg -> llvm_unreachable NVPTXLowerArgs.cpp:256)

title: Sub-byte vector global whose element width does not evenly divide a byte (e.g. <8 x i3>, <2 x i3>) asserts / report_fatal_errors on valid IR
trigger: A module-scope addrspace(1)/addrspace(4) global of a fixed vector type whose element is an integer narrower than a byte but whose width does not divide 8 (i3, i5, i6, i7), with a non-zero constant initializer.
ir: @g = addrspace(1) global <2 x i3> <i3 1, i3 2>, align 1

title: NVPTXLowerArgs ArgUseChecker no-op default misclassifies atomicrmw/cmpxchg/icmp/freeze on byval kernel param as read-only -> llvm_unreachable("Unsupported instruction") crash in convertToParamAS
mechanism: Same root cause as finding 1: ArgUseChecker has no visitInstruction override, so AtomicRMWInst, AtomicCmpXchgInst, ICmpInst (the pointer operand), and FreezeInst all fall through to InstVisitor's no-op `visitInstruction` and are classified read-only (PI neither escaped nor aborted). With NO conditional present, lowerKernelByValParam takes path (1): `if (ArgUseIsReadOnly && AUC.Conditionals.empty())` (line 437) -> convertToParamAS -> CloneInstInParamAS (lambda at line 214). That lambda only handles LoadInst, GetElementPtrInst, BitCastInst, AddrSpaceCastInst, MemTransferInst; for anything else it hits `llvm_unreachable("Unsupported instruction");` (line 256). So the very instructions the checker wrongly waved through as safe crash the cloner. This is the direct sibling/superset of the confirmed round-1 ArgUseChecker icmp/atomicrmw bug, extended across instruction types: atomicrmw, cmpxchg, icmp, and freeze all reproduce the identical UNREACHABLE at line 256. (Note icmp is a borderline miscompile even when it does not crash: under path 2 it compares param-AS pointer values, e.g. `cvta.to.param` of generic-null, changing pointer-equality semantics vs the original generic-AS icmp.)
trigger: A ptx_kernel with `ptr byval` arg used by atomicrmw/cmpxchg/icmp/freeze with no phi/select on the path (Conditionals empty), any target (crashes at sm_50 and sm_90 alike, since path 1 does not depend on hasCvtaParam).

title: NVPTXLowerArgs ArgUseChecker ignores freeze of a byval kernel param -> downstream store invisible, missing local copy (miscompile) / convertToParamAS crash
mechanism: ArgUseChecker does not override visitFreezeInst, and neither does PtrUseVisitor. FreezeInst -> DELEGATE(Instruction) -> visitInstruction (inherited no-op). Worse than the atomic cases: the no-op default does NOT enqueue the freeze's users (unlike visitBitCastInst/visitGetElementPtrInst/visitAddrSpaceCastInst which call enqueueUsers). So `freeze ptr %arg` forwards the byval pointer through but the checker never examines what is done with the frozen pointer. A `store` through the frozen pointer is therefore completely invisible, and ArgUseIsReadOnly is (wrongly) true at line 436. Outcomes: direct `freeze` use -> case 1 -> convertToParamAS() crashes at line 256 (freeze is not a handled opcode); `freeze` behind a select/phi on sm70+/ptx>=7.7 -> case 2 (line 448) -> cvta.param lowering, ReadOnly attr, no per-thread local copy, and the store goes to the shared param-space copy. Verified: PTX for the select case emits `mov.b64 %rd1, k_param_0; cvta.param.u64 %rd2, %rd1; ... st.b32 [%rd4], 42` writing 42 to the shared param memory with no local depot copy; direct case crashes at line 256.
trigger: A non-grid_constant `byval` pointer kernel argument passed through `freeze` and then written via the frozen pointer. Crash if used directly; miscompile if the frozen pointer flows through a select/phi on sm_70+/PTX>=7.7.
llc_cmd: llc -mtriple=nvptx64 -mcpu=sm_90a -mattr=+ptx80 in.ll -o -   (miscompile: @mc_freeze -> cvta.param + st to shared param mem, no local copy); llc -mtriple=nvptx64 -mcpu=sm_70 in.ll -o -   (crash: @crash_freeze -> llvm_unreachable NVPTXLowerArgs.cpp:256)

title: tcgen05.st 16x32bx2 i64 offset immarg truncated to i32 in SelectTcgen05St (miscompile/assert)
mechanism:
In NVPTXDAGToDAGISel::SelectTcgen05St the immediate offset operand is materialized as:

  Operands.push_back(CurDAG->getTargetConstant(
      cast<ConstantSDNode>(N->getOperand(3))->getZExtValue(), DL,
      MVT::i32)); // Offset

The offset is declared as i64 everywhere it matters: the intrinsic class NVVM_TCGEN05_ST in include/llvm/IR/IntrinsicsNVVM.td uses `llvm_i64_ty` for the 16x32bx2 offset and marks it ImmArg, and the instruction operand in lib/Target/NVPTX/NVPTXIntrinsics.td (TCGEN05_ST_INST, line 5939) is `i64imm:$offset`. By choosing MVT::i32 the C++ selection code drops the high 32 bits of the 64-bit immediate. The 16x32bx2 LD path (lowerTcgen05LdRed) keeps the offset as an i64 SDValue and is matched by tablegen against `i64imm:$offset`, so it is correct; only the hand-written ld/st selection truncates. In a release (no-assertions) build, getTargetConstant silently truncates, so e.g. offset 0x100000002 is emitted as `, 2` in the `tcgen05.st.sync.aligned.16x32bx2.* [taddr], <offset>, {...}` instruction -> store to wrong tensor-memory location. In an assertions build it instead trips the APInt `isUIntN(BitWidth,val)` assert (confirmed crash, see llc_cmd).
trigger: Call llvm.nvvm.tcgen05.st.16x32bx2.x* with an i64 immediate offset whose value does not fit in 32 bits (e.g. i64 4294967298 = 0x1_0000_0002).

title: tcgen05.ld 16x32bx2 i64 offset immarg truncated to i32 in SelectTcgen05Ld (known round-1 bug, still present)
mechanism:
NVPTXDAGToDAGISel::SelectTcgen05Ld materializes the offset as:

  auto OffsetNode = CurDAG->getTargetConstant(
      cast<ConstantSDNode>(N->getOperand(3))->getZExtValue(), DL, MVT::i32);

Same defect as the .st sibling: the 16x32bx2 offset is `llvm_i64_ty` ImmArg in IntrinsicsNVVM.td (class NVVM_TCGEN05_LD) and the instruction field is `i64imm:$offset` (TCGEN05_LD_INST, NVPTXIntrinsics.td line 5915), but selection forces MVT::i32, dropping the high 32 bits. This is the original round-1 tcgen05.ld offset truncation; included because it is unchanged in the working tree (git blame: commit f5ee401545076, same commit as the .st path). Release build: wrong offset silently emitted in `tcgen05.ld.sync.aligned.16x32bx2.* ..., [taddr], <offset>` -> reads from wrong tensor-memory location. Assertions build: APInt isUIntN assert in SelectTcgen05Ld (confirmed crash).
trigger: Call llvm.nvvm.tcgen05.ld.16x32bx2.x* with an i64 immediate offset > UINT32_MAX (e.g. i64 4294967298).

title: NVPTXLowerArgs ArgUseChecker misclassifies atomicrmw/cmpxchg on byval kernel param as read-only -> emits atom.param writing read-only param space (no local copy)
lines: 310-383 (ArgUseChecker, missing visitInstruction override), 436-467 (classification consumed in lowerKernelByValParam)
mechanism: ArgUseChecker : PtrUseVisitor<ArgUseChecker> (line 310) overrides visitStoreInst, visitAddrSpaceCastInst, visitPtrToIntInst, visitPHINode, visitSelectInst, visitMemTransferInst, visitMemSetInst, but has NO visitInstruction override. PtrUseVisitor has no handler for AtomicRMWInst/AtomicCmpXchgInst, so they fall through InstVisitor's chain to `void visitInstruction(Instruction&){}` (a no-op) -- PI is neither escaped nor aborted. Thus in lowerKernelByValParam: `const bool ArgUseIsReadOnly = !(PI.isEscaped() || PI.isAborted());` (line 436) becomes TRUE for a pointer that is atomically WRITTEN. When a conditional (phi/select) is present, path (1) (line 437, `ArgUseIsReadOnly && Conditionals.empty()`) is skipped, and on sm70+/ptx>=77 (hasCvtaParam) path (2) fires: `if (HasCvtaParam && (ArgUseIsReadOnly || isParamGridConstant(*Arg)))` (line 448). Path (2) wraps the arg into ADDRESS_SPACE_ENTRY_PARAM and replaces uses WITHOUT making a writable local copy (copyByValParam at line 470 is skipped). The atomicrmw/cmpxchg then operates directly on .param space. Confirmed emitted PTX for atomicrmw add: `mov.b64 %rd1, kernel_..._param_0;` ... `atom.acquire.sys.param.add.u32 %r1, [%rd1], 7;` and for cmpxchg: `atom.acquire.sys.param.cas.b32 %r1, [%rd1], 1, 2;`. Kernel parameters in .param space are read-only; the IR semantics require the per-thread byval copy to be modified, not the parameter. The correct lowering (taken for a plain `store`, which IS handled by visitStoreInst->setAborted) allocates __local_depot, copies param->local, and operates on .local. The downstream NVPTXAliasAnalysis (NVPTXAliasAnalysis.cpp:107-119, isConstOrParam returns NoModRef for ENTRY_PARAM, relying on the comment 'NVPTXLowerArgs also does not allow any writes to .param pointers') compounds this by treating the leaked param write as a no-op for other memory.
trigger: A ptx_kernel with a `ptr byval` argument whose pointer (or a GEP of it) is used by atomicrmw or cmpxchg, with a phi/select on the path (so Conditionals is non-empty and path 1 is skipped), compiled for sm_90 with ptx>=77 so hasCvtaParam() is true and path 2 is taken.
ir:
target triple = "nvptx64-nvidia-cuda"
%struct.S = type { i32, i32 }
define ptx_kernel void @kernel_atomicrmw_cond(ptr byval(%struct.S) align 4 %p, i1 %c) {
entry:
  %g0 = getelementptr %struct.S, ptr %p, i32 0, i32 0
  %g1 = getelementptr %struct.S, ptr %p, i32 0, i32 1
  br i1 %c, label %a, label %b
a:
  br label %j
b:
  br label %j
j:
  %ptr = phi ptr [ %g0, %a ], [ %g1, %b ]
  %old = atomicrmw add ptr %ptr, i32 7 seq_cst
  ret void
}

title: sitofp/uitofp i{16,32,64} -> bf16 lowered as int->f32->bf16 (double rounding) on targets lacking direct int->bf16
trigger: sitofp/uitofp from an integer whose magnitude exceeds 2^24 (so it is inexact in f32) to bfloat, on sm_80/sm_89 with ptx<78 (any subtarget where STI.getSmVersion()<90 || STI.getPTXVersion()<78). Pick an i64 value at a bf16/f32 double-rounding boundary.

title: NVPTXLowerAggrCopies lowers overlapping aggregate load/store pair as a forward (memcpy) copy loop, miscompiling memmove-like IR semantics
lines: 67-122 (collection at 67-80; transform at 105-122; in particular the createMemCpyLoopKnownSize call with /*CanOverlap*/ true at 111-118)
mechanism:
In runOnFunction, any aggregate `load` (>= MaxAggrCopySize=128 bytes, single-use feeding a `store`) is collected (lines 67-80) and lowered with:

  createMemCpyLoopKnownSize(SI, SrcAddr, DstAddr, CopyLen,
                            LI->getAlign(), SI->getAlign(),
                            LI->isVolatile(), SI->isVolatile(),
                            /*CanOverlap*/ true, TTI);

createMemCpyLoopKnownSize (llvm/lib/Transforms/Utils/LowerMemIntrinsics.cpp:390) ALWAYS emits a forward, index-0-to-N, interleaved load-then-store loop. The `CanOverlap` flag only toggles whether noalias/alias_scope METADATA is attached to the generated load/store (see lines 450-462, 495-507 of LowerMemIntrinsics.cpp); it never changes copy direction. So `CanOverlap=true` does NOT make the copy overlap-safe -- it merely avoids emitting a (false) noalias assertion. The emitted copy is still a plain forward memcpy.

The problem: the IR being lowered is `%v = load [N x T], ptr %src; store [N x T] %v, ptr %dst`. Its semantics are memmove-like: the load reads the ENTIRE aggregate into the SSA value %v, then the store writes all of %v to %dst. When %src and %dst overlap (legal, non-UB IR -- aggregate load/store has no non-overlap requirement, unlike llvm.memcpy), the correct result is that %dst receives the ORIGINAL contents of %src. A forward interleaved copy instead clobbers not-yet-read source bytes.

Confirmed numerically: with a 132-byte buffer buf[i]=i, src=offset0, dst=offset4, copy 128 bytes: correct dst[i]=orig src[i] gives buf byte 8 = 4; the forward copy gives buf byte 8 = 0. First divergence at byte 8.

Confirmed via llc (sm_70): the emitted PTX is a loop `ld.b8 %rs1,[src+i]; st.b8 [dst+i],%rs1; i++; setp.lt.u32 %p1,i,128; @%p1 bra` -- load and store at the same index, interleaved, ascending. No src<dst direction check (contrast llvm.memmove of the same size, which correctly emits `setp.lt.u64` and separate forward/backward loops).

Note: this is precisely the round-1 "overlapping aggregate load/store forward-copy" bug; it is still present at HEAD (6d2a90bd8bf3). The fix would be to lower this pair like a memmove (direction-aware), not a memcpy with CanOverlap=true. Intrinsic paths in this file are NOT affected: llvm.memcpy overlap is UB by spec; llvm.memmove goes through expandMemMoveAsLoop -> createMemMoveLoopKnownSize which is direction-aware; sub-128-byte aggregate load/store falls to SelectionDAG which emits all-loads-before-all-stores (memmove-safe).
trigger: An aggregate load of >= 128 bytes whose single use is a store, where the source and destination pointers are in the same address space and overlap at runtime (e.g. %dst = %src + 4). Same-address-space overlap is the realizable case; distinct NVPTX address spaces cannot alias so direction is irrelevant there.
ir:
target triple = "nvptx64-nvidia-cuda"

; Overlapping aggregate load/store. Valid, non-UB IR: the load reads all 128
; bytes of %src into %v, then the store writes %v to %dst. If %dst overlaps
; %src (e.g. %dst = %src + 4), the correct (memmove-like) result is that %dst
; receives the ORIGINAL contents of %src. The backend emits a forward
; interleaved copy loop, corrupting the overlap region.
define void @overlap_aggr(ptr %dst, ptr %src) {
  %v = load [32 x i32], ptr %src, align 4
  store [32 x i32] %v, ptr %dst, align 4
  ret void
}
